claims_disputed.claim: Location, adaptive compression, implicit relations and metadata-first promotion each contribute, and the full pipeline is best.
claims_disputed.reason: Table III is one unlabeled host and one point per variant. The full-pipeline 85.8% matches the Codex large DeepDiscovery mean in Table II, whose three-run band is 80.0–90.0, so the drops to 83.3, 82.2, and 81.5 sit inside ordinary run noise. Location-only at 80.0% is below that host's native 84.2%.

pattern_stance_changes.reason: The metadata-first drop is 85.8% to 82.2% in Table III, smaller than the Codex large DeepDiscovery run band (80.0–90.0) in Table II, so the ablation does not show the cards winning.
Implicit relations drop full recall only 85.8% to 83.3% on one point, and Table I's edge over AST+GraphRAG (92.6% vs 90.4%) sits inside overlapping three-run ranges (88.9–96.3 vs 87.2–94.4).
Removing adaptive compression drops Table III from 85.8% to 81.5% with no repeats. That gap is inside the three-run band of the matching large-set host in Table II.
Selective full-text promotion is not skills loaded on demand, and the only comparison is the same unreplicated metadata-first cell in Table III.

Table I RAG full recall 84.4% (81.5–88.9) meets native Claude Code at the top of its range (85.2–92.6) after a 7-hour, 2.26-billion-token index. That one offline stack loses on the mean; it does not show embedding retrieval hurts in general.

missed_issues: Table I's Claude Code native cell is 88.9% (85.2–92.6) on the 27 medium tasks, but Table II's Claude Code native medium cell on the same task count is 88.2% (86.4–92.2). Those are presented as the same condition and do not match.

Section V-A says coarse localization by compression takes about 70 seconds, against about 225 seconds for broad search, while Table I records DeepDiscovery task-time execution at 13.2 seconds. The two cost stories are not the same measurement.
Section IV-B gives no inter-annotator agreement for the gold file sets. It only says slight expert variation remains possible, on 135 medium and 240 large gold files.

RQ5 and Table IV treat six products as a model-robustness check, but model and scaffold are tied together. The large-set gains are +9.2 for Cline on Sonnet 4.5 and +2.5 for Claude Code on Opus 4.6, so the paper does not separate backend from agent workflow.

The Location score in §III-C includes a domain-lexicon and framework-idiom rule library aimed at this codebase's configuration and injection patterns. The internal full-recall edge over generic GraphRAG can be idiom match, which the 'annotations predate the method' sentence in §IV-B does not rule out.
note: The review is right on the load-bearing problems: Table I ranges overlap, Table IV's medium gains disagree with Table II, the OpenCode medium 90.2% (82.6–91.2) cell cannot be a three-run mean, micro precision stays near 10%, and the SWE-bench host is unnamed while the introduction calls 70.4% the best baseline. I agree that P43 is mixed and that the paired 352/500 to 393/500 result (McNemar p<0.01) is the part worth keeping, at moderate rather than strong. I do not agree that Table III supports metadata cards, graph relations, compression, or progressive disclosure: those drops are single points inside the run band of the host they appear to match. Employer control of the labels justifies a real conflict; I would not call it high, because Qoder with Qwen is one of six hosts and not the one with the largest gain.
